text:
Maria (Eng Ops): Quick Q from the all-hands — are we officially switching to 2-week releases with a mid-sprint hotfix window? Some teams heard this during the roadmap demo and want clarity on how oncall and rollouts will change.

Josh (PM): Not a global mandate. We're piloting a 2-week cadence for the runtime team to iterate faster. Other teams can opt in if they meet the gating criteria. :rocket:

Srini (VP Eng): Short answer: aim for smaller, safer releases where it makes sense. Policy we discussed: default stays 4-week unless a team applies for 2-week with a canary + automated rollback + QA gate. Oncall coverage shifts slightly — teams on a 2-week cadence will move to a per-release rotation for the deploy window. Details below.

Oncall Bot: Scheduled rotation posted: https://intranet.redwood.example/oncall-schedule (pinned) :spiral_calendar:

Devon (SRE): Can we get a concrete definition of the "QA gate" and "quality bar"? Are flaky test counts, perf regressions, or increased 5xxs included?

Anya (Head QA): Quality bar we used in the pilot: no new P0/P1 failing tests, e2e smoke pass, and perf within 10% of baseline for p95 latency on critical flows. Flaky tests must be triaged or quarantined before release. Operationally, infra touches require an ops signoff.

Josh (PM): Canary rollout plan (template): 10% for 30m, 50% for 2h, 100% in 24h with auto-rollback conditions: >=0.5% error rate increase OR p95 latency > target. Teams can tune thresholds but must document rationale.

Devon (SRE): Can we see the rollout config? I want auto-fallback to last-green by default. Also where's the runbook?

Srini (VP Eng): Auto-fallback to last-green is the default for approved 2-week pilots. Runbook link: https://intranet.redwood.example/runbooks/rollout-fallback. We'll also add an ops checklist.

Josh (PM): Sample rollout config (add to PR):

```yaml
rollout:
  strategy: canary
  steps:
    - percent: 10
      duration: 30m
    - percent: 50
      duration: 2h
    - percent: 100
      duration: 24h
  auto_rollback:
    error_rate_pct: 0.5
    p95_latency_pct: 110
  fallback: last-green
```

Anya (Head QA): We'll publish a checklist template and a short doc describing acceptance criteria for 2-week releases. PRs must include the checklist and a perf baseline run.

Maria (Eng Ops): What about SLAs? Will customer-facing SLAs change if we release more frequently?

Srini (VP Eng): No SLA rewrites for customers. Hosted customers continue under existing SLOs; Dedicated/enterprise customers have contract terms. Internally, we expect teams to maintain the same reliability targets — faster cadence doesn't mean accepting worse SLOs.

Devon (SRE): Good. Request: add an automated smoke job that runs post-deploy and posts an explicit status to the release thread. Saves manual check-offs.

Josh (PM): Agree — we'll make the smoke job a required step in the pipeline for any 2-week rollout. It will post results and link the perf baseline.

Maria (Eng Ops): Thanks. I'll update the all-hands notes and share a short FAQ. Can @Oncall Bot pin the pilot schedule and the runbook in #eng-oncall? :thumbsup:

Oncall Bot: Done — schedule and runbook pinned in #eng-oncall.

Srini (VP Eng): We'll run the pilot for two cycles, then review telemetry (deploy failures, rollbacks, customer incidents, and dev velocity). If all looks good, we'll formalize the option. Expect a follow-up doc with the application process for teams.

Josh (PM): Pilot cohort: runtime, eng-platform. Retrospective in ~6 weeks.

Maria (Eng Ops): Awesome — closing the loop here. If anyone has open concerns, drop them in #all-hands-followup or ping me directly. :eyes:
